title: Laboratory Data Logger — Overview and definition
t: Laboratory Data Logger — Overview and definition
description: Records long-duration multi-channel measurements with metadata and alarms.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Records long-duration multi-channel measurements with metadata and alarms. A laboratory data logger samples temperature, voltage, pressure, and other channels on schedules from milliseconds to hours, storing timestamped data with full metadata for months. Real implementations include PicoLog, DATAQ WinDaq, and Python loggers around Modbus/OPC UA. It survives power loss with journaling, backfills from device memory, and exports analysis-ready files.
capabilities: Scheduled and triggered multi-channel logging
Journaled storage surviving power loss and restarts
Backfill from instrument onboard memory after outages
Alarm actions: email, SMS gateway, relay outputs
Metadata capture: operator, calibration dates, test IDs

title: Laboratory Data Logger — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Records long-duration multi-channel measurements with metadata and alarms.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Laboratory Data Logger, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Scheduled and triggered multi-channel logging). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Scheduled and triggered multi-channel logging and Journaled storage surviving power loss and restarts. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Data acquisition (DAQ) software) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
